Same spirit as general post-market autopsy, but the object is ONE sector ETF and its
environment — not SPX.

INPUTS (injected):
1. Morning sector prediction for this sector
2. Channel 1: actual sector ETF open/close/% change; SPY % change; relative return
3. Archived morning ETF context

STEPS (do not skip):
0. FACTS: sector ETF %, SPY %, relative %, path if known
1. What drove the sector today (taxonomy-aligned factors preferred)
2. Audit morning S0–S4 reads against reality (use morning numbers, not post-close
   rewrites of the morning)
3. Interactions / double-count / knowable-at-open test
4. Outliers inside the sector

Evidence: CLAIM/URL/PUBLISHED/QUOTE/SUMMARY format for factual claims.

Object is the **near-session XLP environment**, not SPX and not a stock pick. Channel 1 numbers are used as given.

XLP is a **chronic, broad laggard**: **1d −1.38% vs SPY +0.66% (rel −2.03%)**, 3d rel **−3.71%**, 1w rel **−1.40%**, 1m rel **−8.32%**. Thursday was an outsized anti-FTS day (staples worst sector). That 1d relative smash **already happened**. S4 may confirm it. It is not an independent reason to stack a second notable down day.

Macro panel as it maps here: **ES=F 0.0% / NQ=F −0.19%** (flat, NQ not leading), Finviz cash futures SPX −0.12% / NDX −0.29% / DJIA +0.08%, VIX **14.51** (−0.7) with VIX/VIX3M **0.947 contango**, Fear & Greed **58.2 Greed**, DFII10 **2.34 (+2 bp 1d, −1 bp 1w, −7 bp 1m)**, 10Y **4.66 (+2 bp 1d)**, 30Y **5.18** still elevated, **CL −0.8% / BZ −1.91%**, DXY −0.02% 1d, gold futures mixed (GC=F +1.16% vs Finviz gold −0.77%), Asia **−0.15%**, Europe **−0.72%**, HY OAS 2.67 (tight). 5-day 10Y–SPX corr **+0.26**.

### Channel 2 — required categories

**1. Shared macro → this sector.** This is **not** a second 08-27 NQ-led anti-FTS open. NVDA’s beat/guide is **already public** (News Judge #3) and **already in Thursday’s XLP tape**; Salesforce/software is a **tech** sleeve, not an XLP spine. Channel 1 futures are **flat-to-soft**, with NQ **slightly weaker** than ES — the opposite of the 08-27 trigger (NQ ≥ +0.5% and leading). Sticky July core PCE **3.3%** is T-2 (printed 08-26); do not score it as today’s 8:30 and do not pay the same hawkish fact in S0 and S1. **Warsh Jackson Hole is today ~10:00 ET** — two-sided policy binary (framework/credibility, not a locked hike). **UMich final ~10:00 ET** (consensus **51.0**, matching the 08-14 prelim) is two-sided for staples (08-17): weak sentiment can be a bond-proxy bid **or** another hit to WMT/COST volume — do not one-way it as FTS. No 8:30 claims/PCE today. Oil is **down**, so 08-11 geo/oil does **not** fire. Real yields are only a **+2 bp 1d** tick against a still-easing 1m; 30Y remains in a stress zone — treat as noise/stabilization, not a fresh duration impulse (do not double-count). Same shock once: residual AI/software leadership + XLP lag = **one** anti-FTS overlay **already paid Thursday**. For staples today the map is **relative still soft, absolute not independently confirmed**. S0 stays **0**, not −1.

**2. Spine.**

- **Risk-on rotation away from defensives:** **HIT on the prior tape**, only **PARTIAL this morning** (NQ not ripping; ES flat). Do not re-score Thursday as a fresh S1.
- **Pricing power without volume collapse:** PARTIAL / carried. KO quality bid is old; WMT’s slowest US comps in six years is **stale (08-20)** and already absorbed (08-21).
- **Volume decline accelerating:** PARTIAL / carried. July retail −0.6% and UMich 51 are known; today’s UMich final is expected unchanged. Do not restack as a one-way FTS tailwind (08-17).

**3. Secondary.**
- **Input cost relief (ag, packaging, freight):** **checked, mixed — not a clean HIT.** Crude down is freight/energy relief. Offset: wheat ~743¢ (+43% YoY), corn ~512¢ (+29% YoY), SBS carton +$20/t in August, linerboard hikes teed for September, Drewry WCI still ~$4,473/FEU. Do not full-count oil-down twice.
- **Volume stabilization:** checked, nothing material and new — still the soft-volume regime.
- **Staples earnings / stable margins:** no fresh same-day XLP-weight beat. PG product launches and a KO Zacks upgrade are not session spines. WMT 08-27 insider sale is single-name noise.
- **Private-label vs brands:** **HIT** (structural). Circana/PLMA H1’26: store-brand units ~24%, +0.2% vs national brands −0.5%.
- **Rotation into/out of defensives:** **out** on 1d/3d/1w/1m tape. Premarket XLP ~+0.26% after a −1.38% cash smash is **not** an 08-21 reversal (needs futures ≥ +0.3%; ES is 0.0%).

**4. Breadth / leadership.** Thursday was **not** WMT-only: WMT ~−1.6%, COST also red, staples the worst S&P sector. Large-cap / low-beta **lag**, not high-beta chase and not ETF-up/names-flat. Single-ticker rule: WMT (~10%) is context; COST/PG/KO participated. Do not let one name drive the ETF call.

**5. Flows / positioning.** ETF Channel / Nasdaq (08-26): XLP shares **172.77M → 170.57M**, ~**$190M** week-over-week outflow (~1.3%). ETFdb: 5-day **−$192M**, 1-month **−$220M**. That is **outflow / dry-up**, not a crowded-long extreme (1m rel **−8.32%** is the opposite). S3 cannot confirm a washout bounce today.

**6. Catalysts / calendar.** **No 8:30 ET high-impact print.** Load-bearing event is **Warsh ~10:00 ET** (two-sided). UMich final 10:00 ET (expected 51.0) and Chicago PMI 9:45 are secondary. NVDA is **not** pending. Hormel guidance cut was Thursday’s consumer-color print, not a fresh XLP-weight catalyst — do not restack (08-27).

### Lesson / self-audit
- **08-27 staples (promoted today):** NVDA is correctly treated as **already public**. The **notable** exception does **not** fire: NQ is **−0.19%**, not ≥ +0.5% leading ES. Keep direction **down** on the lagging tape; **do not lift the mild cap**.
- **08-14 outsized-reversal:** score Thursday’s −2% rel smash **once** (S4). Follow-through after an outsized day defaults to **mild**.
- **08-21:** WMT −9% is stale; 08-21 reversal checklist is **off** (ES not ≥ +0.3%).
- **08-17:** retail-earnings week is **closed**; do not turn UMich 51 into a one-way FTS bid.
- **08-12 / calendar:** PCE is T-2; Warsh is two-sided — do not force S0 negative merely because a policy event exists.
- **08-11:** oil down, XLP already lagging — geo/oil down/mild **does not fire**.
- **08-10 / 08-14 mild caps:** flat futures, no fresh staples print → **cap magnitude at mild**. 08-27 taught not to apply those caps when NQ ≥ +0.5% **and** a mega-cap print is live; that conjunction is **false** this morning.
- **08-25 utilities flat-default:** does **not** apply — S1 and S4 are not both 0.
- Same-shock: NVDA + software + XLP lag = **one** anti-FTS factor, already in Thursday’s close.
- Single-ticker: WMT is not the ETF call.
- Divergence: leading sum (S0…S3 = −3) and S4 (−1) **agree** (both down). No leading-vs-tape fight. Trust factors; tape confirms.
- Rolling mag 0.4: keep direction, **shrink confidence**, do not promote to notable.
- Open experiment for this scope: **none**.

**Read:** residual **relative down / contained absolute**. Flat futures and a two-sided 10:00 ET Warsh print cap the band at **mild**. A hawkish Warsh surprise is the main path to a larger lag; a dovish-clarify print is the main path to a flat/bounce. Do not let the pipeline promote notable from a −4 component stack with multiplier ≤1.0.

## 1. What drove the sector

Primary driver was **not** residual Thursday anti-FTS follow-through. It was a **same-day policy + leadership unwind**:

1. **Warsh Jackson Hole (~10:00 ET) printed hawkish.** Inflation still too high; 2% PCE is a firm target; summer readings “better than expected” but “do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved”; “otherwise, we have work to do.” September 25 bp hike odds **35.4% → 57.5%**. 2Y **+12 bp to 4.35%**, 10Y **+5 bp to 4.72%**. That was the session’s load-bearing macro shock.
2. **Thursday’s NVDA/software leadership reversed.** NVDA **−4.61%**, PHLX SOX **−3.5%**, XLK **−1.3%**, Nasdaq **−0.5%**. The 08-27 anti-FTS tape that smashed XLP **mean-reverted**. That mechanically lifted XLP vs SPY.
3. **This was not a clean FTS vs cyclicals.** Consumer discretionary **+1.7%** (AMZN **+3.97%**) and communication services **+1.6%** led. Utilities **−1.1%** (duration) lagged. Staples beat the index as **low-beta / non-semi**, not as a classic safety bid vs cyclicals.

Secondary: UMich final **51.7** vs 51.0 consensus / 51.0 prelim (slight beat, still −6% m/m) — two-sided, not the tape. Chicago PMI **47.1** vs ~57 consensus (sharp miss into contraction) — late-morning color that can support defensives, but Briefing treats Warsh as the main driver.

**Top-weight internals (not the ETF call, context only):** WMT ~+0.45%, COST ~+1.16%, PG ~+0.41%, KO ~+0.67%. Breadth inside the spine was **up**, not WMT-only.
